questions.text: A patient underwent a prolonged abdominal surgery under general anaesthesia, at the termination of the operation the anaesthetic agent was discontinued, and the patient was allowed to breathe air spontaneously. Within a few minutes pt. became cyanosed though his breathing was normal (a) Name the most likely anaesthetic agent used & it belongs to which class of general anaesthetics? (b) What is this phenomenon called & explain the underlying mechanism? (c) How will you prevent such an incident? (d) Enumerate general anaesthetics which are given intravenously.

Write short notes on: (a) Uses and adverse effects of Phenytoin (b) Uses and adverse effects of Opioids (c) Uses and adverse effects of Corticosteroids (d) Cotrimoxazole (e) Are there exceptions to full disclosure? Can family members request withholding of information from patient?

Explain why? (a) Levodopa is combined with carbidopa for the treatment of Parkinson's disease. (b) Fluoroquinolones are not preferred in children and elderly age. (c) Oxytocin is preferred over ergometrine for the induction of labour

An 82-year-old hospitalized patient with creatinine clearance of 25 mL/min has a microbial infection requiring treatment with antibiotics. Which one of the following drugs is least likely to require a dosage adjustment, either a smaller dose than usual or an increased interval between doses?

questions.text: A 30-year-old patient with uncomplicated P. Falciparum malaria from a region with chloroquine resistance is prescribed artemether-lumefantrine. Why is combination therapy preferred over artemisinin monotherapy?
questions.heading: Multiple choice questions.

options.label: a

options.label: b
options.text: It delays development of resistance & improves efficacy

options.label: c
options.text: Lumefantrine increases renal elimination of artemisinin

options.label: d
